title: SOC2 WarGame: Incident Scenarios & Control Gap Notes (Rhea)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal runbook for running a small-scale SOC2 war game: simulate likely incidents, validate detection/response controls, and collect sample evidence. Not a final report — messy notes, things to ask ops/security/eng.

High-level objectives:
- Exercise three realistic incidents that map to CC:3, CC:4 (change mgmt, monitoring, backups, access)
- Identify weak points where evidence is thin or owners unclear
- Produce a play-by-play that can be converted into test scripts and Jira tasks

Scenarios (priority order):
1) Cloud creds exposure: API key leaked in GitHub commit (accidental).
   Hypothesis: Audit logs + secret scanning + key rotation will detect and contain.
   Steps to simulate: commit fake key to a non-prod repo under org, wait for scanner + webhook alerts, then rotate key via automation.
   Controls to check: secret scanning alerts, IAM key rotation runbook, alert routing to on-call.
   Evidence to collect: scanner alert emails, webhook payloads, rotation audit log entries, Slack thread or PagerDuty incident id.
   Gaps / TODO: confirm which repo types are scanned (private vs internal), who owns rotation automation (eng-platform?), file JIRA-SEC-798 follow-up.

2) Model inference denial: sudden spike in latency/500s from a hosted route (model overload).
   Hypothesis: Autoscaling + fallback policy will keep tail latency under SLO; fallback to smaller model logged and routed.
   Steps: replay synthetic traffic using load test tool (non-customer traffic) against staging then small window on dedicated cluster; trigger fallback policy via simulated capacity exhaustion.
   Controls: autoscale policy, per-route fallback mapping, runtime routing logs, per-token cost alerts.
   Evidence: autoscaler events, routing decision traces (trace ids), fallback model spinup logs, metric graphs for latency and error rate.
   Notes: need to coordinate with infra SRE to avoid impacting shared infra; consider using canary pool.

3) Data exfiltration attempt: attacker queries embeddings endpoint to try to reconstruct training data.
   Hypothesis: rate limits + telemetry + eval thresholds will flag anomalous query patterns; privacy policies block bulk export.
   Steps: issue high-volume embedding requests with varying payloads from test client, watch for rate-limit enforcement and telemetry flags.
   Controls: rate limiting rules, request sampling logs, DLP hooks (if any), customer data tagging, retention policies.
   Evidence: rate-limit responses (headers), telemetry alerts, IP blocking entries, decision logs from DLP.
   Open question: who vets training-data provenance for private deployments? add to follow-ups.

Control mapping checklist (quick):
- Access control: owner, evidence path, last review date, sample artifact location
- Change management: PR approvals, deploy window logs, rollback events
- Monitoring/alerting: alert rules, runbooks, on-call rotation roster, incident timelines
- Backup & restore: last backup timestamp, restore test note, tickets for restores

Quick runbook (for each scenario):
- Pre-game: notify stake teams (SRE, infra, platform, legal if PII) + set test window + escalation contacts
- Execute: run steps, tag all test traffic with header X-WARGAME:Rhea-2026, capture full logs/trace ids
- Post-game: summarize timeline, collect artifacts, map to SOC2 control IDs, write recommended remediations + owners

Evidence quality rubric (how I'll grade):
- Directness: logs show action vs inference only (high vs low)
- Tamper-resistance: sealed/immutable source (audit logs) vs ad-hoc screenshots
- Linkability: can map event -> actor -> system -> timeline
- Ownership: clear named owner or ambiguous (bad)

Immediate todos (personal):
- Confirm scan coverage for private vs internal repos (ask DevSec via Slack) -- assigned to Leo
- Book 2-hour blast window with infra (March 9) to run scenario 2 only in canary pool -- ping Maya
- Draft a short template for evidence upload (Confluence) so reviewers know where to look
- Convert this doc into 3 Jira test-cases (one per scenario) with expected artifacts checklist

Questions to resolve / chat prompts:
- Are rotation scripts part of eng-platform or product infra? (if eng-platform, need their sign-off)
- For hosted customers: how do we separate test traffic from customer telemetry in long-term storage? TTL or tag-based filtering?
- What's the current policy for simulated secrets placed in repos for tests (allowed? safety checks?)

Notes to self (messy):
- Keep war-game small: 3 scenarios max in first run. Focus on detection/ownership, not long remediation steps.
- Want at least one evidence artifact that is immutable (audit log entry w/ id).
- If legal will be involved (PII risk), get pre-approval.

Appendix: quick links
- Confluence draft for evidence upload: CONFLUENCE-CT-4421
- Related ticket: JIRA-SEC-798 (follow-up key rotation owner)
- Slack threads: #trust-ops / thread pinned March-2026

End of notes — clean this up after run and move to shared drive / shared_drives/company/misc for audit trail.
